function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I don’t personally know anyone named Daniel—my knowledge is based on publicly available information up to my last update. If you’d like, I can help craft a friendly introduction or greeting for someone named Daniel. Just let me know what details you’d like to include (e.g., his relationship to someone else, whether to mention that relationship, etc.) and I’ll generate it for you!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "do you know Daniel?" We need to respond appropriately. According to policy, we should not claim personal knowledge or relationships. We can say we don't personally know Daniel. We can ask if they want to introduce him. We can also offer to generate an introduction greeting if they provide details. So we should respond politely, clarify we don't have personal knowledge, and ask if they'd like help generating an introduction greeting.
